tspan.tspan: OSC on an objects animation is
In Oscilla, cues make score elements interactive by assigning them an XML id that follows a compact
microsyntax format. This format encodes animation, timing, and trigger logic directly within the
SVG, enabling complex, time-based behaviors without additional scripting.
Supported cue types include:pause(...), stop(...), speed(...), audio(...), media(...), text(...),
repeat(...), traverse(...), choice(...), seq(...), osc(...), page(...), nav(...), button(...),
group(...), rotate(...), scale(...), metro(...), and stopwatch(...), among others.
All cues must include a unique uid parameter, placed at the end of the cue argument list. This
ensures reliable playback behavior, synchronization across clients, logging, and remote triggering
When the playhead intersects an element containing a cue id, Oscilla parses the microsyntax and
triggers the corresponding event. Cues can also be activated manually via buttons, keyboard
shortcuts, or external inputs such as OSC, WebSocket, or MIDI messages.For a full reference of cue
types, syntax rules, and usage examples, see docs/cues.md.
stop() requires manual intervention to restart the score. Hitting space bar or the PLAY button in
the control bar will restart the score. It can also be restarted by incoming OSC message.
pause(dur:4, count:true, uid:p3) pauses playback for 4 seconds and then automatically resumes. In
the score itself, this cue is typically attached to a small square or other marker which can be
visible or invisible. The performer does not see the microsyntax — it lives only in the SVG id. The
expression is shown here for clarity in this help file.

tspan.tspan: navigation and mode control within OscillaScore. Unlike cuePage, which handles timed page
sequencing and automated playback, cueNav is primarily used to let performers or conductors
manually control the flow of the score. It can switch between scroll and page modes, jump
directly to specific pages, move forward or backward, restart or stop a running playlist, or
even trigger other cue types like cueAudio() or cueText() as part of a single action. For
example, cueNav(mode(scroll)) exits page mode, while cueNav(replace(page5)) stops the current
In short, cueNav acts as a control interface layer — it doesn’t sequence content over time
like cuePage, but provides responsive user-driven control over navigation and state
transitions during a performance. ... to control page mode from inside a page (or anywhere),
* Exit page mode back to scrolling mode
* Chain actions like “stop then trigger a new cuePage(...)”

order = seq (in order) | rnd (shuffled, loops by default)
dur = seconds per unit or range (e.g. 1-3)
gap = pause between units or range
hold = final visible hold before fade-out
fade = fade duration (ms or % of dur)
loop = repeat count; 0 or inf = infinite
target= center (default), self (cue position), or element ID
offsetX / offsetY = pixel offsets from target

sequencing cues; syntax and behavior may change without notice.
cueSeq chains multiple cues into timed sequences that
unfold automatically. Each item can reference any cue
by its _uid, with timing modifiers like :2
in waits (wait(2)), loops, and random choices
(rand(a,b,c)) to create dynamic, branching cue flows.
The sequencer waits for each cue to finish before
advancing—unless marked parallel—making it perfect for
This plays a 1 s wait, then introText, starts noise in
parallel, overlaps synth by 2 s, randomly picks
between page1 or page2, then plays outroAudio, looping

tspan.tspan: Oscilla features two complementary paradigms — Page Mode and Score Mode. Though distinct in function,
these modes can interconnect and reference each other within a single project.
By default, each project opens in Score Mode, presenting a continuous, time-based scrolling score. A
portal to Page Mode can be initiated either at the outset to bypass scrolling entirely or at any point
within the score to introduce page-based branching and navigation.
Page Mode follows a familiar button- or hyperlink-based navigation structure, suited to modular or
Score Mode provides a media-player-style control bar with standard playback and navigation functions.
Double-click or tap anywhere on the score to bring up or hide the control bar.
Use the [A] button in the control panel to bring up the
rehearsal mark navigation interface (keybinding R) or
use the chevron buttons in the control bar.
Toggle the visibility of score annotations
using the notes button in the control bar.
Oscilla uses standard SVG files created in Inkscape as its native score
format. Composers and designers can build visual layouts, add cue objects,
and embed microsyntax directly within the SVG using Inkscape’s XML Editor.
Once saved, the file can be loaded in the browser-based Oscilla player, where
all cue logic, animations, and interactions are automatically parsed and
This workflow allows artists to compose visually in Inkscape while
maintaining real-time, executable control structures in the browser —
ensuring a seamless transition from graphic score design to interactive
How to Add or Edit Cues in Inkscape
In most examples, the microsyntax defining a cue is attached
to the XML id of a text element, which often also displays
To add or edit a cue (or any other microsyntax-based feature):
- Select the object you want to edit.
- Press Ctrl + Shift + X to open Inkscape’s XML Editor.
- Edit or insert the desired microsyntax in the object’s id field.
Microsyntax can be attached to any SVG object, not just
text elements. Objects carrying cues may also be hidden
or non-visible, allowing invisible triggers and control points
To get started with Oscilla, all you
need is a single project folder
a score.svg file at its top level —
this is the main scrolling or page-
based score that Oscilla loads on
media such as text cues, audio,
video, or images, these must be
scroll modes. You can use the
You can open Oscilla in your browser at

If no target is set, fade applies to self.
Set osc:1 to send OSC messages (/oscilla/fade/<uid> value); use osc:0 to mute per cue.
Global OSC can also be muted via window.OSC_ENABLED = false.
in, out, inout, pulseSlow, pulseFast, strobe, blink, stop:
fade(mode:inout,dur:2,from:0,to:1) → Fade in then out once (2 s total)
fade(mode:in,dur:2,ease:easeOutQuad) → Smooth fade-in with gentle deceleration
fade(mode:pulseSlow,from:0.3,to:1,time:10) → Smooth slow pulse for 10 s, then stop.
fade(mode:pulseFast,ease:easeInOutSine) → Fast rhythmic pulse with smooth curve
fade(mode:blink,dur:0.5,from:0,to:1) → Hard on/off blink every 0.5 s (120 BPM, no easing)
fade(mode:blink,dur:0.5,delay:2,time:8) → Start blinking after 2 s, run 8 s then stop
fade(mode:pulseFast,hold:0.2,delay:1) → Wait 1s, then pulse with 0.2 s pause between cycles
fade(mode:blink,dur:0.5,uid:blink37,osc:1) → Blink sending OSC updates for UID “blink37”
fade(mode:in,dur:2,uid:fadeA,osc:1) → Fade in over 2 s and stream OSC fade values for UID “fadeA”

tspan.tspan: value = speed multiplier (1 = normal, 0.5 = half, 2 = double)
add = relative adjustment to current speed (+/-)
ease = easing curve for ramp (optional, defaults to linear)
uid = unique identifier required for synchronization
speed(add:0.1, uid:s3) // slightly + than current speed
speed(value:1.3, dur:4, uid:s4) // ramp to 1.3× over 4 seconds
speed(add:-0.2, dur:2, uid:s5) // - gradually over 2 seconds
speed(3, uid:s7) // same as speed(value:3, uid:s7)

The microsyntax appears only in the SVG id field.
Creates an interactive HTML/CSS button in the score
that triggers a cue when clicked.
Buttons provide a manual activation method, in
The cue expression must include its
style() = visual and behavioral settings for the
toggle = if true, clicking again sends a corresponding stop/toggle action (when supported)
uid = unique id for the button element itself (required for sync, logging, and OSC control)
style(size:"120x45", color:"#333", textcolor:"#fff", fontsize:36, active:"flash", uid:btnNoise)
- The performer sees only the button graphic; microsyntax remains in the SVG id.
- `toggle:true` is useful for start/stop pads or continuous textures.
- Use Inkscape’s Align and Distribute to arrange multiple buttons cleanly.
Navigates to a page, rehearsal mark, or scroll mode location.
The first argument determines the navigation action. It may be:
scroll = switch to scrolling mode and continue playback
scrollPaused = switch to scrolling mode but do not resume playback
<pagename> = jump directly to a page or rehearsal mark
The optional @<target> is used when scroll mode needs to jump to a specific place.
actionOrPage = "scroll", "scrollPaused", or a page/rehearsal name (e.g., page3, Coda, Intro)
target = optional rehearsal/page anchor used only with scroll modes
uid = unique cue identifier (optional unless this exact nav expression appears more than
nav(page3, uid:p3) // same, with explicit uid
nav(scroll@A) // enter scrolling mode and jump to A
nav(scrollPaused@B) // jump to B and hold playback (no auto-resume)
nav(scroll) // switch to scroll mode, do not jump
nav(scrollPaused) // switch to paused scroll mode in place
UID is optional unless the same nav() expression is used more than once or in a button().
If a nav cue needs to be referenced, retriggered, or logged uniquely, add uid:<name>.
The performer sees only the visual cue symbol in the score.
The microsyntax remains in the SVG id and is not shown in the visible notation.
allows reusable clusters of visual or interactive elements to be defined once and re-used anywhere else
in the score. Any SVG group (<g>) whose id begins with reuse- is treated as a reusable block. For
example, a group named reuse-menu or reuse-controls might contain cueButtons, cueText labels, arrows,
symbols, or any combination of UI elements or animated objects.
To recall the block elsewhere in the score or inside a page, create a placeholder object with an id of
the form use(name). When the score loads, each placeholder is automatically replaced with a cloned
instance of the block reuse-name. The cloned content inherits the position of the placeholder, so
placement is controlled visually in Inkscape without additional scripting. Updates to the original reuse-
name block propagate to all uses, preventing duplicated elements from drifting apart over time.
This supports building modular, consistent score UI structures: navigation menus, helper panels, graphic
symbols, repeated annotations, instrument instructions, dynamic prompts, and other reusable visual
fragments. The composer edits the source once and places it wherever needed throughout the score.
use(menu) — clone at placeholder position (default; recommended)
use(menu)@self — clone exactly where the placeholder is drawn, for precise overlay work
use(menu)@sticky — clone and keep the block on-screen (for HUD overlays; future option)
• The cloned instance receives a unique ID to prevent collisions.
• Animations and cue interactions inside the block are re-initialized automatically.
• If a reuse-name block is not found in the current page, the system searches other pages
and the main score until a definition is located.
The below panel is defined once in pages/ui.svg as reuse-menu and recalled here automatically
using use(menu) at the placeholder location.
Loads a named SVG page from `/pages/` and pauses the scrolling score.
Useful for shaping form, branching structure, guided transitions, and non-linear navigation.
Pages may persist until another cue, or auto-advance using durations or SC-style patterns.
page-pattern constructs following the semantics of **SuperCollider Patterns**
(sequences, random with/without repetition, shuffle once, reshuffle each cycle, choose one).
- `page(page1:5)` → show page1 for 5 seconds, then return.

text.tspan: Controls visual rotation of any SVG object around its transform origin. Rotation may be continuous or driven by a list or
pattern of angles. To use rotation, assign an object (usually a <g>) an id of the form rotate(...).
The first parameter may be given or not rotate(values:[0,120,240], dur:4) OR rotate([0,120,240], dur:4)
In the implicit form, the first argument (a list or pattern) is treated as the values sequence. This keeps simple forms short
while still supporting named parameters for clarity.
Rotation occurs in place. The pivot defaults to the object’s visual center, but may be adjusted in Inkscape via Object →
Transform → Center, or by setting transform-origin in the style. Proper pivot placement prevents visual drift.
mode:once play the sequence once and stop
interp:step angles jump instantly; dur controls step spacing
hold:0.4 optional pause after each smooth step
In smooth mode, hold applies after reaching each step. In step mode, hold is ignored and dur acts as the per-step delay.
Patterns supported for values and durations:
Pxrand([ ... ], inf) random, no immediate repeats
osc:2 send one OSC message per completed step
rotate([0,120,240], dur:4) Cycles three orientations every 4 seconds.
rotate([0,90,180,270], dur:0.5, interp:step) Snaps through quarter-turns twice per second.
Alternating direction with independent rhythmic pattern.
rotate(dir:1, dur:1) Continuous clockwise rotation (one turn per second).
rotate(values:[0,180], mode:alternate, dur:1, osc:1, uid:180) WITH OSC SEND
BUGs; MINUS VALUES DOENT PARSE CORRECTLY!
any examples including a - minus get passed through to the fallback clockwise rotation
pencil and shapes fine but bezier tool marks with only straigt line translates
off screen perhaps due to bounding box being 0

rect.id: rotate(values:Pxrand([0, 120, 240, 60, 45, 180], inf), dur:Pseq([2, 0.6, 1], inf), interp:smooth, hold:0.4 )

path.id: rotate(values:Pxrand([0, 120, 240, 60, 45, 180], inf), dur:Pseq([2, 0.4, 1], inf), interp:smooth, hold:0.4 )
rotate(values:Pxrand([0, 120, 240, 60, 45, 180], inf), dur:Pseq([2, 0.4, 1.2], inf), interp:smooth, hold:0.4 )

tspan.tspan: Controls motion of any SVG object along a target <path>, supporting continuous, reverse, ping-pong, and node-based traversal. Use
o2p(...) on any object to animate it. The first parameter selects the path: o2p(path:ring, dur:4) or the implicit form o2p(ring,
dur:4). Objects follow exact SVG path geometry; origins are auto-normalised so the object sits precisely on the curve even under
mode:forward (fwd) move start→end (default) • mode:reverse (rev) move end→start
mode:alternate (alt) ping-pong between endpoints • mode:jumpNodes hop between actual path nodes (evenly sampled)
dur:4 seconds per traversal (A→B or A→B→A if alternate) • loop:0 infinite (0=forever, n=stop after n cycles)
start:0.0 fractional start offset (0–1, trims front of path) • end:1.0 fractional end offset (0–1, trims tail of path)
rotate:1 follow path tangent direction for natural orientation (ideal for arrows/pointers/vehicles)
rotate:0 disable tangent rotation (default). Rotation is computed from local dy/dx at each frame.
ease:n or "name" uses same easing system as rotate()/scale(); affects progression along path distance, not speed of transform.
osc:1 enable continuous OSC: /obj2path <uid/path> <normX> <normY> <angle> • osc:0 off (default)
Normalised coordinates (0–1) map to path bounding box; angle is tangent heading in degrees. Ideal for spatial audio, diffusion
mapping, DMX, robotics, or multi-node systems.
Closed <path> elements orbit seamlessly with zero discontinuity at the join; heading wraps smoothly; OSC angles follow true
circular geometry (0° = top, clockwise). Perfect for speaker arrays, ring lights, robot arms, kinetic sculptures, rotating spatial
sources, or radial motion graphics. No special mode required—any closed path becomes an orbit automatically.
Assign uid:myObj to gain persistent animation identity. Later calls, e.g., o2p(uid:myObj, mode:alt, dur:6), update the running
animation in place without recreating or resetting the object. Supports dynamic score changes, adaptive timing, OSC-driven control,
o2p(path:ring, dur:6) → continuous orbit around entire path
o2p(path:ring, mode:alt, dur:3) → ping-pong traversal A↔B
o2p(path:orbit1, rotate:1, osc:1) → tangent-aligned orbit with spatial OSC
o2p(path:line1, start:0.2, end:0.8, dur:2) → restrict motion to middle segment
o2p(path:wobbly, mode:jumpNodes, dur:2) → hop between node positions on the curve
o2p(path:orbit1, uid:orb, dur:4) → create persistent controllable animation
o2p(uid:orb, mode:rev, dur:5) → live-update to reverse direction mid-score
o2p(path:ring, mode:fwd, loop:0) → infinite forward looping
Controls visual scaling of any SVG object around its transform origin. Supports uniform and non-uniform (X/Y-separate) sequences,
smooth or stepped interpolation, loop/once/alternate modes, and SuperCollider-style patterns (Pseq, Prand, Pxrand, Pshuf) for
values and durations. Use scale(...) or scaleXY(...). The first parameter may be explicit (scale(values:[1,1.5,1],dur:2)) or
Pxrand([...],inf) random no repeats • Pshuf([...],inf) shuffled list
Patterns work for: values in scale(), x/y in scaleXY(), and dur: patterns.
interp:smooth tween between values (default; hold applies)
interp:step jump instantly between values (hold ignored; dur = step delay)
dur:1 seconds per step or pattern element
hold:dur*0.25 pause after each tween (smooth only)
ease:"name" any Anime.js easing (linear / easeInOutSine / etc.)
pauseOnExit:1 once-mode ends at final value (0 = revert to first)
Used when no explicit sequence is provided; generates a cyclic pulsing animation.
Useful for mapping scale to audio, diffusion, lighting, robotics, CV/OSC instruments, etc.
scale([1,1.5,1],dur:2,interp:step,osc:2) → stepped scaling with per-step OSC
scaleXY(x:Pxrand([1,1.3,1.6],inf), y:Pshuf([1,0.8,1.2],inf), dur:1) → alternating randomised X/Y cycles
